notes.title: Dyer's Report and Warning
items: Professor William Dyer summoned the investigators to his Miskatonic University office and asked them to help stop Dr. Amy Kensler's planned follow-up expedition to Antarctica.

The university's public account of Dyer's previous expedition had reported little of scientific value, but his newly revised report revealed the truth he had deliberately withheld in the hope of keeping others away from the polar ice.

Dyer supported his testimony with photographs, sketches, academic papers, and field records showing mangled and dissected bodies, five-pointed snow graves, unfamiliar specimens buried beneath the ice, and aerial views of jagged black mountains surrounding an ancient stone city.

He described that city as the work of primordial beings known as Elder Things and warned that renewed drilling, excavation, and melting of the ancient ice could expose forces humanity was not prepared to understand.

Danforth, the only other survivor known to have reached the city with Dyer, paced the office in an agitated state and muttered about a nameless black pit, lending a disturbing human weight to Dyer's account.

notes.title: The Debate
items: The investigators found Dyer's evidence detailed and difficult to dismiss, yet the scale of his claims made complete belief almost impossible.
Dyer argued that scholars eventually reach boundaries science should not cross and that Dr. Kensler's party might never return if it followed the same route.

The investigators answered that Kensler had taken precautions and that learning what truly waited beneath the ice was the only way to understand the threat and prepare for future expeditions that might be far less cautious.

Danforth questioned whether the horrors remembered from the earlier expedition were real or the product of exhausted minds. Dyer sharply replied that his deepest concern was not the distant mirage but the terror he had witnessed in Danforth himself during their escape.
Chosen response: "I believe you... but if what you say is true, should we not investigate these findings further?"

Unable to persuade the investigators to abandon the journey, Dyer reluctantly agreed that he and Danforth would accompany the expedition, both to protect the party and to confront what they had left behind.

notes.title: Campaign Consequences
items: Record in the Campaign Log: the investigators convinced Dyer to allow the expedition.
Add 1 cultist token to the chaos bag for the remainder of the campaign.

notes.title: Departure aboard the Theodosia
items: At Boston Harbor, the investigators joined the expedition aboard the Theodosia while its crew loaded scientific equipment, supplies, aircraft components, and the team's sled dogs.
Dr. Amy Kensler, a Miskatonic biology professor and the expedition's disciplined leader, checked off each arrival while remaining determined to proceed despite Dyer's objections.
Roald Ellsworth, a veteran of more than a dozen expeditions, brought practical field experience and immediately helped move luggage and equipment aboard.
James "Cookie" Fredericks, the ship's forceful and hardworking cook, focused on finishing preparations before departure and showed little patience for delay.
Takada Hiroko joined as the aeroplane mechanic responsible for assembling and maintaining the expedition's aircraft after arrival in Antarctica.

Avery Claypool, an associate of Ellsworth, would serve as the Antarctic guide. An unresolved dispute between the two men was obvious when they met at the gangway, though Kensler expected them to work together.

Dr. Mala Sinha came aboard as the physician responsible for frostbite, hypothermia, gangrene, and the expedition's other medical dangers. Her exchange with Kensler revealed a personal unease beneath their professional relationship.
Eliyah Ashevak arrived with Anyu and took responsibility for the sled-dog team: forty-four dogs in addition to Anyu, making forty-five in total.

Professor William Dyer and Danforth arrived last. Dyer made clear that he had joined to keep Kensler and the others alive, while Danforth remained compelled to return despite the trauma of his earlier journey.
The remaining travelers were students, researchers, and independent explorers who completed the broader expedition aboard the ship.

notes.title: Nine Campaign Partners
items: These nine characters are the campaign's partners. Their physical injuries, mental strain, deaths, or insanity must be tracked throughout the expedition.
Proceed to Scenario I: Ice and Death.

notes.title: Eight Weeks South
items: Eight long and difficult weeks after leaving Boston, the Theodosia followed the route once taken by the Arkham and the Miskatonic: south along the eastern coast, through the Panama Canal, and onward toward the Antarctic Circle.

The weather grew steadily colder as the ship approached Antarctica, and increasingly frequent icebergs made navigation hazardous. The crew's experience and the surviving logs of earlier captains nevertheless allowed the expedition to maintain good time.
At last, the mist-covered peaks of Mount Erebus and Mount Terror appeared on the horizon. They marked Ross Island and the nearby ice shelf that would serve as the expedition's landing point.

notes.title: Preparing to Make Landfall
items: Dr. Amy Kensler assembled the expedition team on the deck of the Theodosia and explained that they would use the same breeches-buoy system as the previous expedition to transfer supplies from the ship onto the ice shelf.
James "Cookie" Fredericks, Roald Ellsworth, and Avery Claypool were assigned to take one of the smaller boats ahead and locate a safe landing zone on the shelf.
Once camp was established, Takada Hiroko was to make assembling and preparing the expedition's aeroplanes her first priority.

Eliyah Ashevak and the sled dogs would move supplies from the landing site to camp. Expecting a great deal of work in very little time, Kensler ordered him to have the dogs ready before landfall; Eliyah answered with dry obedience while petting Anyu at his side.

notes.title: The Purpose of the Expedition
items: Professor William Dyer noticed that the expedition had brought no ice-melting or drilling equipment and sarcastically asked whether Kensler had abandoned any plan to collect mineral samples.

Kensler replied that mineral collection was not their primary mission. Their purpose was to corroborate what Dyer and Danforth had discovered, and to return with stronger evidence of the ancient species they had named the Elder Things.

Kensler went further: if the expedition found a suitable specimen, she considered bringing back a living Elder Thing an ideal outcome, comparing such a discovery to finding a living woolly mammoth preserved in the ice.

Dyer reacted with alarm, reminding her that the creatures had killed several members of Lake's party and demanding to know how she expected to capture one. Kensler coolly answered that he was the expert and should tell her; furious, Dyer walked away muttering that the expedition had been a bad idea from the beginning.

notes.title: Approaching the Ice Shelf
items: Kensler dismissed the meeting with the warning that they would reach land within the hour and that everyone must be ready to begin work immediately.
When the investigators pointed out that they had not yet been given a specific assignment, Kensler replied with a faint smirk that there would be more than enough manual labor to go around.
Proceed to Scenario I: Ice and Death, Part I.

storyNotes.title: Scenario I: Ice and Death, Part I

notes.title: Into the Mountains
items: After two weeks of exhausting work on the ice shelf, Takada and the mechanics completed three aeroplanes. The investigators prepared to fly two of them over the jagged mountains and photograph the ancient stone city described in Dyer's report.

Kensler planned to establish a temporary outpost if the flight discovered a safe landing zone. Dyer, Danforth, Fredericks, and Claypool would remain there while the rest of the expedition returned to base camp and used the sledges to move supplies between the two camps.

The two aircraft took off into low visibility and violent Antarctic winds. As the storm abruptly intensified, the planes were tossed through the sky and forced toward the ground despite Claypool's warning that they had to turn back.

Moments before the crash, the passengers glimpsed an immense dark shape stretched across the mountains like a curtain or the tattered wings of some ancient creature. It watched them with hollow eyes and reached toward the aircraft before everything went black.

The investigators regained consciousness inside the burning wreckage and were dragged into the snow. Most of the expedition team survived with only bruises, but James "Cookie" Fredericks was killed in the plane crash.

notes.title: The Death of Cookie
items: Roald Ellsworth and Avery Claypool knelt beside Cookie's body. Claypool called him a good man, and Ellsworth agreed that Cookie had been one despite his many attempts to make the others believe otherwise.

Kensler interrupted their mourning and insisted that the survivors had to keep moving. Eliyah objected, but Claypool accepted that she was right, saying Cookie himself would have been the first to tell everyone not to dawdle.
Cross James "Cookie" Fredericks off the Expedition Team. Record that he was killed in the plane crash.

notes.title: The Disappearance
items: The investigators' sleep at Remnants of Lake's Camp was plagued by the murderous cold, the ceaseless wind, and nightmares of misshapen black forms erupting from beneath the frozen ground.
A startled cry ended their rest. They awoke to find the camp in disarray and several companions missing, with footprints leading away from the shelter and into the Antarctic night.

Because the camp had Shelter 7, seven surviving expedition partners were randomly declared safe: Professor William Dyer, Eliyah Ashevak, Dr. Mala Sinha, Avery Claypool, Dr. Amy Kensler, Roald Ellsworth, and Takada Hiroko.
Danforth was the only surviving partner not among the seven safe members and was recorded as MIA.
The investigators chose to go after the missing team member and play the next part of the scenario, but decided to take a break before continuing.
Proceed to Scenario I: Ice and Death, Part II.

storyNotes.title: Scenario I: Ice and Death, Part II

notes.title: Searching for the Missing Expedition
items: After only a brief refuge from the lethal Antarctic cold, the investigators prepared to follow the tracks leading away from Remnants of Lake's Camp and search for Danforth, the expedition's only missing survivor.

The disappearance made little sense: no supplies had been taken, nobody had seen Danforth leave, and the weather offered almost no chance of surviving the night alone. The team feared that something alien had compelled him to walk into the frozen wilderness.
Add 1 frost token to the chaos bag for this continuation of Ice and Death.
Because the camp's Shelter value was 7, each investigator's base starting resources were 7 instead of 5.

notes.title: The Expedition Team Responds
items: Dr. Amy Kensler reacted to the disappearance with anger and immediately prepared to lead the search. Because she was alive and not missing, she would enter play with 1 additional secret if chosen as a partner.

Professor William Dyer recognized the crisis as a repetition of Professor Lake's lost expedition. Danforth's disappearance left him exhausted and guilt-ridden, convinced that he should have taken his student's warnings more seriously.
Because Danforth was missing, Professor William Dyer had to accompany an investigator if able; he would enter play with 1 additional secret.

Avery Claypool confirmed that none of the missing expedition's supplies had been taken and warned that an unprepared traveler could not survive the night in the current weather, especially with unknown creatures still roaming the ice.
James "Cookie" Fredericks' conditional passage did not apply because he had already been killed in the plane crash.

notes.title: The Attack
items: The investigators had barely begun to rest when something erupted from beneath the nearby ice. Tremors split the ground around the camp, followed by the insidious piping cry of "Tekeli-li! Tekeli-li!"

The creatures encountered earlier had evidently risen from somewhere deep below Antarctica's glacial crust. As the quakes intensified, the investigators imagined the monsters bursting from the ground, crawling into their bodies, and taking control of them.
With the camp no longer safe, the investigators chose to stand and fight rather than flee from the attacking creatures.

items: The investigators chose to proceed to Ice and Death, Part III immediately.

notes.title: The Hunting Creatures Advance
items: The expedition moved just outside the camp to find a defensible position and saw more hunting creatures emerging from the ice by the minute.
The ice shelf split open and multicolored miasma seeped from the cracks in a succession of geysers. With no safe route left, the investigators prepared to fight.
Add 1 frost token to the chaos bag.

notes.title: The Expedition Presses On
items: The surviving expedition members took stock of their situation. Although several companions had been lost, the team remained strong enough to continue.

Abandoning the expedition empty-handed would damage the university, frustrate the scientific community, and threaten the careers of the remaining crew. The investigators therefore chose to press onward despite the unanswered questions surrounding the phantasmal creatures.
Another flight was out of the question after the crash and the sighting of the entity in the sky. The expedition would continue toward the site described in Dyer's report on foot.
The investigators had time to check on three expedition members and chose Danforth, Professor William Dyer, and Avery Claypool.

notes.title: Team Members Checked On
items: Danforth recognized the entity that struck down the aircraft as the same thing he had seen during his earlier expedition. Listening to him grants further insight: any one investigator may begin Scenario II: To the Forbidden Peaks with two additional cards in their opening hand.

Professor William Dyer compared the spectral creatures' ethereal physiology with the flesh-and-organ bodies of the Elder Things and wondered about the connection between them. Because at least one deck contained Tekeli-li weaknesses, any one investigator could remove up to five Tekeli-li weaknesses from their deck.
Avery Claypool analyzed the abnormal Antarctic storms and advised moving during the first break in the weather. Remove 1 frost token from the chaos bag.
Because Roald Ellsworth was also alive, Claypool admitted that Ellsworth's stubborn, solitary nature made closeness difficult for both of them—but worthwhile.

storyNotes.title: Scenario II: To the Forbidden Peaks

notes.title: The Journey to the Mountains
items: Ursula Downs, Preston Fairmont, and lead investigator Marion Tavares set out across the frozen tundra toward the distant jagged peaks. The party traveled in uneasy silence, still shaken by the horrors of the previous days.

Eliyah Ashevak was alive and Wooden Sledge had been recovered. He secured the provisions and equipment to the sledge and prepared Anyu and the dogs for the journey. The investigators suffered no ill effects.

Avery Claypool was alive. He led the party across the ice, checking its thickness with an auger and warning everyone to watch for cracks and sudden changes in weather. The investigators suffered no ill effects.
Takada Hiroko was alive. She shared a song her father had taught her, and the expedition sang together as they traveled. The investigators suffered no ill effects.
The investigators had not scouted the mountain pass. The recorded journey imposed no ill effects, although the snow, rough terrain, and fierce wind made progress slow.

Near the foot of the mountains, the party discovered a frozen, half-buried Elder Thing. Its leathery wings, star-shaped head, and tentacles matched the beings described by Dyer and Danforth, but the cause of its death was unknown.

notes.title: Resolution 1: The Summit
items: All three investigators survived. From the summit, they saw the ancient city from Dyer's report: a labyrinth of dark stone buildings concealed beyond the mountains. After the losses suffered during the climb, the achievement felt hollow.
The expedition began descending toward the city, planning to make camp before reaching the bottom.

items: The expedition made camp in a silence deepened by its losses. Unable to rest, the investigators checked on their companions.

No investigator had physical trauma and no partner had recorded damage, so this conversation had no healing effect and did not count toward the three-conversation limit.

notes.title: Remembering Cookie
items: A member of the expedition brought over Cookie's belongings, including a damaged pocketwatch, a matchbook from the Excelsior Hotel, and his well-maintained revolver.
Preston Fairmont added Cookie's Custom .32 to his deck as a story asset. It costs no XP and does not count toward his deck size.

notes.title: Roald Ellsworth
items: Ellsworth took an investigator down the mountain slope to scout a half-buried building on the outskirts of the city.

When they returned, Claypool rushed to greet Ellsworth, relieved that he was safe; the two reconnected.

notes.title: Interlude Results
items: Three effective conversations were completed: Claypool, Cookie, and Ellsworth. Sinha's conversation granted an additional choice because there was nothing to heal.
Fatal Mirage had not been completed, but fewer than three expedition members were crossed out. Proceed to Scenario III: City of the Elder Things.

storyNotes.title: Scenario III: City of the Elder Things

notes.title: Into the Alien City
items: Beyond the peaks, the investigators confronted a vast city of towers, temples, bridges, and pyramids unlike anything built by humanity. Dr. Sinha reminded everyone to protect themselves from the cold and stay hydrated.

Because the investigators had scouted the city outskirts with Ellsworth, they led the expedition through the half-buried structure they had found the previous night. Dyer warned them to remain alert to whatever might dwell behind the ancient walls.

Inside, they found the freshly mutilated bodies of Elder Things. Their escape route was blocked by ice and rubble, and without Cookie they spent longer finding another way out and suffered further exposure.

notes.title: The Expedition Chooses a Route
items: Group Two had the most surviving members: Danforth, Takada Hiroko, and Eliyah Ashevak. Their vote led the expedition along the mountain ridge toward a region Dyer and Danforth had never explored.

notes.title: Scenario Interlude: Gaze into Madness
items: The app randomly selected Takada Hiroko as the victim. Drawn by whispers, she listened at a wall and opened a door containing a terrible, churning miasma.
The others closed the door while averting their eyes. Takada collapsed; her heart continued to beat, but she never regained consciousness. Cross off Takada Hiroko in the Expedition Team.

notes.title: Resolution 1: The Hidden Tunnel
items: All three investigators survived. The expedition entered a secret passage and descended into an unnaturally quiet shaft, following strange markings deeper beneath the city. Despite their doubts and the danger to their sanity, they pressed on in search of answers.
Record in the Campaign Log: the team found the hidden tunnel.

notes.title: Fourteen Hours Underground
items: The expedition rested in a dark pit beneath the city. Without sunlight, time had become impossible to judge; the group was shocked to learn that fourteen hours had passed since going underground.

notes.title: Kensler's Research
items: The investigators examined the research left behind by Dr. Amy Kensler, hoping her notes could explain what they had encountered. Among her belongings was a journal documenting the journey and the expedition's early days in Antarctica.
Marion Tavares added Kensler's Log to her deck as a story asset. It costs no XP and does not count toward her deck size.

notes.title: Roald Ellsworth
items: Ellsworth invited an investigator to explore the icy depths with a lantern and icepick. Moving ahead of the larger party, they scouted the route together.
Record in the Campaign Log: the investigators scouted the forked passage.

notes.title: Avery Claypool
items: Claypool noticed that the underground cold was unnatural: even without windchill, it was colder than expected. A fleeting shadow moved within the ice, alarming both him and the investigator.
Claypool's predictions helped the expedition avoid the unnatural cold. Remove 1 frost token from the chaos bag.
This conversation counted toward the three-conversation limit. No additional conversation was granted, and the investigators did not check on Takada Hiroko.

notes.title: Into the Mirage
items: As the investigators tried to sleep, an instinctive sense of danger roused them. Instead of the underground camp, they found themselves inside an unfamiliar yet strangely familiar hall.
The investigators chose to open the door and venture into the mirage.
